steps.body: Division follows the SAME sign rule as multiplication: same signs give a positive quotient, different signs give a negative quotient. -20 ÷ 4: different signs, so -5.

commonErrors.feedback: Different signs give a NEGATIVE quotient: -20 ÷ 4 = -5.

explanationVariants: Same signs (both negative) give a positive quotient: -18 ÷ -3 = 6.
Two negatives divide to a positive.

commonErrors.feedback: Same signs give a POSITIVE quotient: -18 ÷ -3 = 6.

steps.body: Division undoes multiplication — if -4 × 3 = -12, then -12 ÷ 3 = -4 and -12 ÷ -4 = 3. The sign rule stays consistent both ways.

widget.prompt: -12 ÷ 3 = ? Drag the marker to the quotient.

commonPlacements.feedback: Different signs give a NEGATIVE quotient: -12 ÷ 3 = -4.

widget.successFeedback: Different signs: 12÷3=4, negative: -4 — the missing factor sits left of zero.
widget.lowFeedback: That landing is further left than the quotient. 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so the answer is 4 units left of zero.
widget.highFeedback: That landing is right of the quotient. A negative divided by a positive lands on the negative side.

predict.prompt: −12 ÷ 3 asks: 3 times WHAT gives −12. That missing factor's sign is…

options.label: Negative — a positive times it must land negative

predict.reveal: 3 × (+4) = +12, the wrong side of zero — only 3 × (−4) reaches −12. Division inherits multiplication's sign rule because it IS a multiplication question in reverse: different signs in, negative out.
